subject.title: Feature: Handle Signal message edits (editMessage envelope)

question: Should a Signal message edit only update/edit-mark transcript context, or should it also cancel/supersede an active turn that began from the original message?
rationale: Current main has a partial native-reply linkage but no durable semantics for transcript replacement, inbound dedupe, or an in-flight turn; choosing that behavior affects user expectations and the boundary with the broader cancellation proposal.

options.title: Adopt a bounded Signal edit contract
options.body: Keep the change in the Signal plugin, carry both timestamps as explicit edit metadata, update or annotate transcript context, and suppress a new group turn unless the edit explicitly mentions the agent.

options.title: Include active-turn cancellation
options.body: Define edits as a cancellation-and-rerun signal, which requires a shared, cross-channel run-control contract and should be coordinated with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/55691.

options.title: Retain ordinary inbound treatment
options.body: Keep the existing generic inbound behavior and document that Signal edits may create a new turn, accepting duplicate-context risk.

recommendation.title: Adopt a bounded Signal edit contract
recommendation.body: Keep the change in the Signal plugin, carry both timestamps as explicit edit metadata, update or annotate transcript context, and suppress a new group turn unless the edit explicitly mentions the agent.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Signal inbound monitor and its routing/dispatch behavior have the strongest history connection to this area.
